legal.demoNotice: This document is placeholder text for a demonstration interface. It is not a legal agreement, it has not been reviewed by a lawyer, and it must be replaced with counsel-drafted terms before any real deployment.
legal.terms.title: Terms of service
legal.terms.intro: The terms on which SportGo would be offered. Placeholder text for a demonstration.
legal.terms.s1.p1: An account would be available only to people who are at least 18 years old, resident in a jurisdiction where the service is licensed, and able to enter a binding contract. Age would be verified by a licensed provider before any wager or deposit — not by a checkbox.
legal.terms.s2.p1: One account per person. You would be responsible for keeping your credentials secret and for all activity on your account. Accounts found to be shared, sold or opened on someone else's behalf would be closed.
legal.terms.s3.p1: A bet would be accepted only once confirmed by the server. Prices displayed in the browser are indicative; the price recorded server-side at acceptance governs. Settlement would follow the official result published by the competition organiser.
legal.terms.s3.p2: In this demonstration a bet is placed against your credit balance: the stake is deducted at once and the ticket is settled by an operator from the result of each selection. No real money is involved.
legal.terms.s4.p1: Deposit, stake, loss and session limits, cooling-off periods and self-exclusion would be available at all times. A reduction takes effect immediately; an increase is held for a cooling-off window. Self-exclusion cannot be lifted before it expires.
legal.terms.s5.p1: SportGo is a demonstration and carries no licence, so it offers no service, makes no promise and accepts no liability. Nothing here creates a contract.
legal.privacy.title: Privacy policy
legal.privacy.intro: How personal data would be handled. Placeholder text for a demonstration.
legal.privacy.s1.p1: Your account details (username, display name, country), your password as an Argon2id hash, your sign-in sessions, and the ledger and betting records of your credits. No e-mail address or phone number is collected. There is no analytics and no tracking. IP addresses are kept in the audit log for security investigations.
legal.privacy.s2.h: What a real deployment would collect
legal.privacy.s2.p1: Identity and contact details, verification records, transaction and betting history, device and session information, and communications. Each purpose would need a lawful basis, a retention period and a route for you to exercise your rights.
legal.privacy.s3.p1: Card details would never reach SportGo. A PCI-DSS compliant provider would collect them through hosted fields or a redirect, and only a provider token and a masked label would be stored.
legal.privacy.s4.p1: Access, rectification, erasure, restriction, portability and objection — subject to the record-keeping a gambling licence and anti-money-laundering law require.
legal.cookies.title: Cookie policy
legal.cookies.intro: Which cookies this build sets, and why.
legal.cookies.s1.p1: sportgo_locale stores your language and sportgo_theme your theme. sportgo_session keeps you signed in (an opaque identifier; the server stores only a hash of it) and sportgo_csrf protects forms against cross-site requests. All are strictly necessary, expire, and none is shared.
legal.cookies.s2.p1: No analytics, advertising, profiling or third-party cookies are set. Because none are set, this build shows no consent banner — a banner that asked permission for nothing would be theatre.
legal.help.title: Help centre
legal.help.s1.p1: The money is not: balances are demonstration credits. Accounts, balances, bets and transactions are real records, and what you do here is really recorded — but no real money moves and no bet is placed with a betting operator.
legal.help.s2.p1: Not online: no payment provider is connected. An operator records deposits on your account, and a withdrawal request holds your balance until an operator approves or declines it.
legal.help.s3.h: Why does my account not verify my age?
legal.help.s3.p1: Accounts are created by a manager, not by you, and nothing in this build checks anyone's age or identity. Real age verification requires a licensed provider checking a date of birth against an authoritative source, and this build has none. Whoever creates an account is responsible for confirming the holder is of legal age.
legal.help.s4.h: Where can I get support for gambling harm?
legal.help.s4.p1: The responsible gambling page explains the tools and what support a licensed operator must provide. No helpline number is published here, because inventing one would be worse than publishing none.
legal.contact.title: Contact
legal.contact.intro: This is a demonstration project. There is no support desk behind this address.
legal.contact.s1.p1: A licensed operator would publish a support address, a postal address, a company registration number and a licence number here, along with the regulator's complaints route.
legal.about.title: About SportGo
legal.about.intro: What this project is, and what it deliberately is not.
legal.about.s1.p1: SportGo is an interface and architecture study for a sportsbook built for the Tunisian market: French, Arabic and English, right-to-left as a first-class direction, Tunisian competitions first, and the dinar's three decimal places respected in the data model.
legal.about.s2.p1: It is not a gambling operation, it holds no licence, and it must not be presented as one. Every regulated capability — pricing, settlement, payments, identity verification, self-exclusion registers — exists here as a typed boundary with a refusing implementation behind it.
